title: A Drupal workflow-state hook produces an approval trail distinct from node revisions
content:
The integration is a Drupal hook on workflow state change, dispatching a typed operation for a public-sector approval. The claim is a separation: the approval trail is distinct from node revisions.

This is the third appearance of the same distinction in this part of the corpus. Alfresco records versions rather than decisions, Nextcloud cannot tell a sign-off from a move, and Drupal's revision history records content edits rather than approvals. In each case the tool has a detailed change log and still cannot answer what a change meant, which is what makes the record-layer argument portable across content systems rather than specific to one of them.

The single lead is publicplan GmbH in Duesseldorf, marked "2 · next". The public-sector framing matters for the demo: an approval on a government content workflow is the case where the difference between "this page changed" and "this was approved for publication" has consequences outside the organisation.
